title: Define PRD acceptance cadence and legal sign-off matrix for rolling feature slices
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: PRD reviews are a source of friction for rolling releases. Legal often becomes a bottleneck when entire PRDs are submitted for sign-off; design and engineering have different expectations for the level of detail required. Goal: define a repeatable cadence and lightweight sign-off matrix that lets product ship vertical feature slices ("rolling slices") with clear gates and SLAs while preserving legal/compliance coverage for data handling and export controls. Deliverables: a cross-team playbook, a PRD template with mandatory acceptance fields, a legal sign-off matrix (roles + SLAs), a lightweight onboarding checklist for design/eng reviewers, and two pilot PRDs to validate the cadence.
acceptance_criteria: Playbook doc published in Confluence and approved by Product, Design, Eng, and Legal owners
Sign-off matrix lists approver roles (Owner, Eng TL, Design Lead, Legal Reviewer) and SLA targets (standard: 5 business days, expedited: 48 hours)
PRD template added to repo with explicit acceptance criteria and privacy/data sections; template merged to docs repo
Two pilot rolling-slice PRDs completed end-to-end using the cadence; one pilot with low-risk data changes, one with moderate data-sensitivity; both achieve target SLAs
Automation tasks (PRD checklist checks and reviewer ping) created and triaged as ENG tickets for next sprint
notes: Trade-off: shorter legal SLAs speed delivery but increase risk of missed contractual/data obligations — mitigated by a triage rubric to route high-risk changes to full legal review
Design prefers a single canonical PRD template to reduce back-and-forth; engineering wants minimal mandatory fields to avoid blocking work intake
Proposed expedited lane for bugfixes and UI copy changes that do not touch data/export surfaces
Consider integrating sign-off state into Console's route release UI later to reduce manual handoffs
decisions: Adopt two-tier SLA for legal: expedited (<=48h) for low-risk rolling slices; standard (<=5 business days) for anything touching data residency/KMS/export controls
Require an explicit 'data risk' checkbox and short rationale in every PRD before legal review is requested
Design review must sign off on 'UX acceptance' before engineering requests legal to avoid rework
Pilot cadence: submit PRD Monday, design and eng review by Wednesday, legal gated on Thursday unless expedited flag set
